section.title: Objective and Overview
section.para: The goal of this mission is to show how to target a transfer trajectory from an Earth parking orbit to a Mars orbit via B-Plane targeting. Given an inclination target for the Sun-centered transfer, we solve for the velocity of the spacecraft in certain directions in order to determine a transfer trajectory.

Construct, run, save and reopen your own mission first. Then compare its settings with the historical reference MarsBPlaneTutorial.script. The reference uses older resource names and some more precise values; the differences described below are intentional.

listitem.para: Basic understanding of B-Planes and their usage in targeting a position.
Tutorials:
Objective: Target a Martian transfer trajectory using B-Plane Targeting, to achieve a transfer inclination of 24.677° in the SunMJ2kEq coordinate system before the Mars encounter.
Assume:
Parking orbit SMA = 10000 km
Parking orbit ECC = 0.1
Find:
INC
BdotT
BdotR

section.title: Creating and Configuring the Resource Tree
section.para: In the Qt GUI, start a new mission and use the Resources tree. The existing DefaultSC and DefaultProp can be renamed MarsSupply and EarthProp with F2; create the other resources with the tree's Add commands. Resource forms use Apply and update the active script. Propagator forms edit the integrator; the associated Force Models entry edits CentralBody, PrimaryBodies and PointMasses. Output contains the current OrbitView and ReportFile resources. The older illustrations below remain useful for their parameter values, although their wx dialog labels differ.

For this tutorial, four impulsive burns are used to maneuver a single spacecraft, and three propagators are used for different portions of the spacecraft's propagation. The propagators use different point masses to account for the dominant gravity fields during the spacecraft's trajectory. Two OrbitView plots are used to track the path at the starting point and ending point of the mission. Finally, four coordinate systems are used to define the spacecraft's position - based, accordingly, on Earth, Mars, the ecliptic, and the equatorial plane of the Earth.

listitem.para: Spacecraft: MarsSupply
Impulsive Burns: TOI, MarsMCC, MarsBPlane, and MarsOI
Propagators: EarthProp, SunProp, and MarsProp
Differential Corrector: MarsTOIDC
Plots/Reports: EarthView and MarsView and a data report
Coordinate Systems: MarsMJ2000Eq, SunMJ2kEc, SunMJ2kEq, and EarthSunRot
Spacecraft
Add a spacecraft to the resource tree and rename it MarsSupply
Set the epoch format to TAIModJulian
Use an Epoch of 21160
Set the State Type to Keplerian
See Assumptions to modify spacecraft element properties
Propagators

Remove all primary bodies and gravity models from all propagators. In each associated Force Model set PrimaryBodies to an empty list, then configure CentralBody and PointMasses: Earth/Earth for EarthProp, Sun/Sun, Earth, Luna for SunProp, and Mars/Mars for MarsProp. This removes the default Earth gravity field rather than leaving it alongside the point masses.
EarthProp

Use RungeKutta89, InitialStepSize 60 sec, Accuracy 1e-12, MinStep 0.001 sec, MaxStep 86400 sec and MaxStepAttempts 50, as shown in the EarthProp illustration. For SunProp and MarsProp the original prose omits Accuracy; this walkthrough retains the current creator default 1e-11, with RungeKutta89, InitialStepSize 60 sec and MinStep 0.001 sec. Keep StopIfAccuracyIsViolated true.
Include only a Geocentric point mass
SunProp
Set the Integrator max step size to 160000 sec
Set the Integrator max step attempts to 500
Include heliocentric, geocentric, and lunar point masses
MarsProp includes only a martian point mass
Set the Integrator max step size to 86400 sec
Set the Integrator max step attempts to 100
Burns

Create four ImpulsiveBurn resources with CoordinateSystem Local and Axes VNB. In the current form V, N and B are Element1, Element2 and Element3 respectively. Leave unspecified elements zero and DecrementMass false; TOI uses Origin Earth.
Change the TOI vector V to 2.85 km/s
Change the MarsMCC vector N to - 0.8593 km/s with a heliocentric origin
Change the MarsBPlane vector V to - 0.3309 km/s and B to 0.6917 km/s with a heliocentric origin
Change the MarsOI vector V to - 4 km/s with a martian origin
Coordinate Systems
EarthSunRot
Set the Type of Axes to ObjectReferenced

Make Sun the Primary body and Earth the Secondary body. Set Origin Earth, XAxis R, leave YAxis blank, and set ZAxis N, as shown in the illustration. ObjectReferenced axes expose these settings directly in the current form.
SunMJ2kEc
Apply a heliocentric origin to the system
Use MJ2000Ec as the Type of Axes
SunMJ2kEq
Apply a heliocentric origin to the system
Use MJ2000Eq as the Type of Axes
MarsMJ2000Eq
Apply a martian origin to the system
Use MJ2000Eq as the Type of Axes
Solvers

Create a DifferentialCorrector named MarsTOIDC in the Solvers folder. Retain the current defaults: ShowProgress true, ReportStyle Normal, MaximumIterations 25, DerivativeMethod ForwardDifference and Algorithm NewtonRaphson.
Set ReportFile to targeter_MarsTOIDC.data in an existing writable output directory. This is the current name of the older Targeter Text File setting.
Plots/Reports

Create a ReportFile named Data in Output. Set Filename to Ex_MarsBPlane.report in an existing writable output directory, Precision 16 and ColumnWidth 20. Leave Add empty: the Report commands below supply the parameter list. Retain SolverIterations Current and the other report defaults.

Create an OrbitView named EarthView in Output. Use EarthMJ2000Eq for CoordinateSystem and ViewUpCoordinateSystem, Earth for ViewPointReference and ViewDirection, a ViewPointVector of [0 0 30000], ViewScaleFactor 1 and ViewUpAxis Z. Include MarsSupply and Earth.
Add Sun to the Objects list
Set Grid and SunLine to On

Create an OrbitView named MarsView. Include MarsSupply and Earth, then add the bodies below. Set ViewPointReference and ViewDirection to Mars, ViewPointVector [0 0 30000] and ViewUpAxis Z, as shown in the MarsView illustration.
Add Sun and Mars to the Objects list
Use MarsMJ2000Eq coordinate system in the View Definition and View Up Definition group boxes
Use a View Scale Factor of 2
Set Grid and SunLine to On

section.title: Creating and Configuring the Mission Sequence
section.para: This mission begins at the spacecraft orbit's Earth periapsis point, then moves to a Mars transfer trajectory, and ends in an elliptical orbit about Mars. The transfer trajectory calls two targeting sequences, one to obtain an inclination, and the other to obtain a B-Plane position. In the first targeting sequence, the inclination is achieved, and is then used when the second sequence targets a distinct B-Plane parameter. After the second targeting sequence is accomplished, the spacecraft is slowed by a final maneuver that puts it into the elliptical orbit and continues to propagate for another 25 days. During each Propagate and Maneuver command before and after the targeting sequences, reports are added for tracking and analysis purposes, to monitor the spacecraft's Cartesian coordinates and velocity vectors.

note.para: The original overview and historical reference use a half-day final coast, while the detailed Propagate 6 instruction below specifies 25 elapsed days. This walkthrough follows that detailed instruction. The 24.677° target is the SunMJ2kEq transfer inclination in Target 1; the final MarsMJ2000Eq orbit inclination is a different quantity.

section.para: Use the Mission tree's Insert before, Insert after and Append inside branch commands with the typed forms. The current Assignment template is the older Equation command. Apply each command and save the active script. Configure Target commands with MarsTOIDC, SolveMode Solve, ExitMode DiscardAndContinue and ShowProgressWindow true. Place each Vary, Maneuver, Propagate and Achieve inside its Target branch, with the report following EndTarget. The current Vary variables use burn Element1/2/3 names; the numerical V/N/B meanings remain the same.

listitem.para: Initial Propagate and Maneuver Sequence
For Equation 1, adding a report automatically turns the headers on, so be sure the setting is off to avoid including unnecessary text in the report.
Propagate 1 simply propagates the spacecraft to Earth's periapsis.

Maneuver 1 applies a ΔV in the V direction, to propel the spacecraft for 160 days through Propagate commands 2 and 3. When the propagators switch, the dominant point mass gravity field changes from Earth to Sun.
Targeting Sequences

Target 1 includes Vary, Maneuver, and Achieve commands, to prompt GMAT into achieving the desired inclination. The maneuver applies the MarsMCC impulsive burn to achieve a ΔV in the N direction, so the spacecraft can reach 24.677° and begin its final maneuver.

Target 2 includes two Vary, two Propagate, two Achieve, and one Maneuver commands, to target a BdotT of 10,000 km and BdotR of – 10,000 km about Mars' periapsis. The maneuver applies the MarsBPlane impulsive burn, to achieve a ΔV in both the V and B velocity directions.
Final Propagate and Maneuver Sequence
Maneuver 4 applies a ΔV in the V direction, to slow the spacecraft to the velocity that is necessary to obtain an elliptical orbit about Mars.
The final command, Propagate 6, propagates the spacecraft for an additional 25 days, so the plot can show the entire elliptical trajectory around Mars.

section.title: Running the Mission
section.para: You have now configured the mission, and it is time to run it and see the results. First, save the changes you've made and then click the Run button (green arrow on the tool bar) to run the mission. The screen capture below summarizes what you should see after correctly completing this tutorial. Confirm convergence of both Target sequences: Target 1's SunMJ2kEq.INC residual must be within 0.001°, and Target 2's BdotT and BdotR residuals within 50 km. The data file contains nine rows after its initial header, with seven finite values per row.

Use Mission summary and select MarsMJ2000Eq from the visible coordinate-system drop-down to inspect the final Mars-relative orbit. A positive SMA and eccentricity between zero and one confirm the ellipse. In the qualified walkthrough the final SMA was about 8334.16 km, eccentricity 0.475753 and MarsMJ2000Eq inclination 46.5188°; these are readbacks, not new targeting goals. Save your mission and reopen it to confirm that the resources and command settings were retained before consulting the historical reference.
